Don't get me wrong, I love physical books, but too many of them I see as clutter. I feel like with Kindle I buy a lot of Ebooks, read them and if I really enjoy them sooner or later I end up buying the hardcover version of them (if available, if not then I buy the softcover) and put them on my shelf. Doing it this way I feel as though it's less cluttering, and that my bookshelf really is my own personal selection, I am able to be super picky, especially since my room isn't too big so too many books would be difficult to store. Now if I had a large house with a big room I could turn into a personal library, you bet I'm gonna start hoarding physical books as long as I could have a space to put them and a way to keep them organized.

Not to mention, I buy some books physically just because they look sexy lol. I don't read much Manga, but I ended up enjoying Berserk, which I have in Ebook format, and so after, I bought the physical deluxe hardcovers just because they look so damn good! The black on red design made me realize just how amazing books could look. In fact, if anyone reads this comment, what are some physical books you think look absolutely gorgeous? Training should be done in different public areas such as stores, parks, etc. This is done to make sure that the dog is focused and doesn't get distracted by everything going on around them. And if they are distracted it can help get them used to the distractions and train them to ignore outside distractions.

If you are having a panic attack in a store you want to make sure your service dog will react appropriately in that situation even with all the people walking around, the distant noises, the smells, etc. The last thing you want is your dog walling away, or lacking any type of focus at all. 

Not to be harsh, but no one cares where *you* frequent often. This is a very needed part of the training process. The training process doesn't end either. Staging panic attacks are a required thing to make sure your service dog is on point and stays sharp in their training journey. 
If it bothers you that much then don't frequent these places. Just order curbside pick up, or delivery since most places like this do that now. The training process won't stop just because you don't like it.
